explanation: x86-64's addressing modes define how instructions access operands in memory.  Understanding these modes is crucial for efficient memory access and writing optimized assembly code. Different addressing modes offer trade-offs between code size and instruction execution speed, impacting overall program performance. Efficient use of addressing modes is key to optimizing memory accesses and thus overall program performance.

extraction_metadata.source: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)

book: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective (3rd Edition)
code_example:
; Immediate
mov rax, 0xFACEB00C

; Register
mov rbx, rax

; Register Indirect [BASE]
mov rcx, [rdx]

; Base + Displacement [BASE + DISP]
mov rax, [rbp - 0x18]

; Base + Index [BASE + INDEX] (Scale 1)
mov rax, [rsi + rdi]

; Base + Index * Scale [BASE + INDEX * SCALE]
; Scale must be 1, 2, 4, or 8
mov r8, [r10 + r9*8] ; Array of 64-bit items

; Full Complex Mode [BASE + INDEX * SCALE + DISP]
mov r11, [r12 + r13*4 + 0x20]

; RIP-Relative (64-bit default for data/PC-relative)
mov rax, [rip + 0x012345] ; Accesses global variable
keywords: x86 addressing modes, x64 memory access, assembly addressing, memory operand access
